item.title: Incarico post-doc: Endocrine and Nutritional Modulation of Mitochondrial Adaptations and Metabolic Plasticity: Multi-Omics and Bioenergetic Approaches (Univ. SANNIO (BN))
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-05 12:00
Institution: Univ. SANNIO (BN), Benevento
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-06 Fisiologia

The research programme aims to investigate the cellular and molecular mechanisms through which endocrine and nutritional factors modulate mitochondrial function and metabolic plasticity under physiological conditions and conditions of impaired energy homeostasis. Research activities will focus on the characterisation of bioenergetic adaptations, mitochondrial quality control processes, and signalling pathways involved in tissue responses to endocrine, metabolic, and nutritional perturbations. item.title: Incarico post-doc: Multimodal analysis of functional and structural brain correlates in neurodegenerative diseases: a study of patients and healthy controls (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-28 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-06 Fisiologia

This project investigates how sleep impairments disrupt the brain's glymphatic system, which clears metabolic waste during deep sleep, thereby promoting the accumulation of amyloid-beta plaques and tau proteins associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD). It aims to address a critical knowledge gap in how impaired glymphatic clearance, interacting with broader AD risk factors, predicts clinical onset and disease progression, with a specific focus on cortical hyperexcitability and subclinical epileptiform activity detected via resting-state EEG (rsEEG) and linked to accelerated cognitive decline

Institution: Stazione Zoologica "Anton Dohrn" di Napoli, Napoli
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-04 Anatomia, biologia cellulare e biologia dello sviluppo comparate

The research program aims at investigating the molecular and cellular mechanisms through which the neurosecretory brain–gut axis regulates physiology and behavior in the sea urchin Paracentrotus lividus. Research will focus on the functional analysis of sensory and neuroendocrine pathways controlling ciliary beating, larval locomotion, feeding, swimming behavior, and vertical migration in the water column. Selected components of these pathways will be perturbed at the gene, protein, and pharmacological levels, and their effects will be assessed through cellular, physiological, and behavioral analyses. The research program aims at reconstructing the neural connectome associated with the brain–gut axis in the sea urchin Paracentrotus lividus and understanding how sensory information is integrated to generate physiological and behavioural responses. PMs are potential targets for improving crop performance: efficient dissipation of excess energy can enhance tolerance to abiotic stress, but excessive activation can unpair growth. item.title: Incarico post-doc: Role of Schwann cells within tumour microenvironment in liver cancer and melanoma (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-02 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Rome
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-12 Anatomia umana

Study of the contribution of peripheral nerves to processes of neovascularisation associated with tumour growth, through structural, ultrastructural and immunohistochemical analyses in experimental models and in humans. The role of Schwann cells within the tumour microenvironment in liver cancer and melanoma will be analysed. The project will focus on the capacity of Schwann cells in modulating tumour angiogenesis and vascular mimicry which are essential steps in governing tumour growth, survival and invasion.
